name: National Garden Water Decision Tool
mission: Turn public weather, evapotranspiration, soil and crop data plus the gardener's own irrigation input into a defensible daily watering decision, amount and next-check time.

valueFunctions.description: Water / wait / check soil / hold for rain decisions follow the modeled root-zone state and do not contradict known user inputs.
Balances effective water inputs against crop evapotranspiration within a realistic root-zone reservoir.
Uses rainfall amount and timing; probability is never treated as rainfall depth.
Uses an authoritative reference-ET signal such as NWS FRET when available, with explicit fallback behavior.
Accounts for soil water-holding capacity and crop/rooting depth without pretending point soil data are exact.
Crop and growth stage materially change coefficients, rooting assumptions and stress sensitivity.
The model never assumes it knows whether the gardener irrigated; user-entered irrigation and rain-gauge totals override modeled assumptions.
Avoids unnecessary irrigation when sufficiently large, sufficiently imminent rain is expected.
Raised beds and containers are modeled separately from in-ground soil; NRCS yard soil is never applied blindly to container media.
Returns a clear action, inches to apply, gallons when area is known, reason and next-check time.
Shows freshness, assumptions, confidence and authoritative sources without claiming measured soil moisture.
Supports genuine watering-intent long tails without thin city/ZIP doorway pages.

lossFunctions.description: Issues a watering decision that ignores a supplied recent irrigation or rain-gauge value.
Treats precipitation probability as expected/actual rainfall depth.
Claims actual/measured soil moisture when no sensor or gardener observation supplied it.
Uses NRCS mapped yard soil as if it described container or potting media.
Recommends meaningful irrigation immediately before a high-confidence rain event sufficient to cover most of the modeled deficit without explaining why.
Presents a generic one-inch-per-week rule as a precise local answer.
Uses stale or fallback weather/soil inputs without surfacing freshness or confidence.
Recommended application materially exceeds modeled root-zone refill or ignores obvious shallow-root/container constraints.
Shows many weather numbers but fails to produce a clear watering decision and amount.
Creates templated city/ZIP doorway pages with little unique value.

releaseScenarios.expected: WAIT or CHECK SOIL when the user logged enough irrigation to cover the current modeled deficit.
Higher crop-water demand than cool/cloudy conditions; mature tomato demand exceeds seedling demand but application is capped by root-zone refill.
Sandy soil has a smaller usable reservoir and typically reaches a watering trigger sooner than clay/loam under the same water-out history.
HOLD FOR RAIN when imminent forecast precipitation is large enough to cover most of a near-threshold deficit.
Never converts 70% PoP into 0.70 inches or any rainfall amount.
Raised-bed modifier increases drying/monitoring pressure without inventing measured soil moisture.
Container logic uses potting-media/profile assumptions or explicit user input, never mapped NRCS yard soil.
CHECK SOIL FIRST or reduced confidence when auto soil lookup is unavailable/ambiguous and no manual texture is supplied.
One inch over one square foot converts to approximately 0.623 gallons; amount conversions are regression tested.
Decision explicitly states the assumption that no recent irrigation was logged rather than treating that assumption as observed fact.

releaseGates: All veto loss functions are zero.
Weighted score is at least 92/100 and every critical value function scores at least 85.
Unit tests cover water balance, rainfall timing, crop stage, soil reservoir, user irrigation override, container separation and gallon conversion.
API contract tests verify NWS/NRCS fallbacks and freshness labels.
Production browser smoke enters a ZIP, selects a crop/stage, records recent irrigation, submits, and verifies decision + amount render on desktop and mobile.
Canonical, assets and API are verified through https://chrisizworski.com rather than only through the child Vercel project.
Garden hub links to the tool only after production smoke is green.
